title: Practical One
text:
Calculate Beta estimate
Here, Y is the response variable, and X is the design matrix. The cars data (an R data set, also always available in R) contains two variables: speed and distance to stop. Fit a simple linear regression model to these data, i.e. find the beta estimates, using the equation above, and matrix calculations in R.
Code

####### Create design matrix ####### 
Y <-cars$dist
intercept<- rep(1, length(Y))
X <- cbind(intercept,cars$speed)

#######  Function Calculates Beta hat and Std Error ####### 

calculate <- function(X, Y){
  
  beta_hat <- solve(t(X) %*% X) %*% t(X)%*% Y
  
  # Calculate Std Errors
  Sxx <- sum((X[,2] - mean(X[,2]))^2)
  Sxy <- sum((X[,2] - mean(X[,2])) * (Y - mean(Y)))
  
  predictions <- beta_hat[1]+beta_hat[2]*X[,2]
  residuals <- Y-predictions
  rse <- sqrt(sum(residuals^2)/(length(Y)-2))
  
  se_intercept<- rse*sqrt(1/length(Y)+mean(X[,2])^2/Sxx)
  se_speed <- rse/ sqrt( Sxx)
  
  # Display Std Errors
  std_error <- matrix(0, 2, 1) 
  std_error[1,1] <- se_intercept
  std_error[2,1] <- se_speed
  
  return( list("coefficients" = c(beta_hat[1], beta_hat[2]), 
               "std error" = c(se_intercept, se_speed)))
}


#######  Results ####### 
answer <-calculate(X,Y)

Question 2
Define a function customLowess(x, y, f) that returns the smoothed values.
Code

##### customLowess Function #####

customLowess <- function(x, y, f) {
  
  y_ans <- numeric(length(x))
  
  # Calculate the span
  k <- f * length(x)
  
  for (i in 1:length(x)) {
    
    dist <- abs(x - x[i])
    
    # Determine max distances point of k points
    neighbours <- order(dist)[1:k]
    max_dist <- max(dist[neighbours])
    
    # Calculate weights
    weights <- (1 - (dist[neighbours] / max_dist)^3)^3
    ifelse(any(weights[dist[neighbours] > max_dist]), 
           weights[dist[neighbours] > max_dist] <- 0,weights <- weights)
    
    # Weighted linear regression
    X <- cbind(1, x[neighbours])  
    W <- diag(weights)  
    Y <- y[neighbours]  
    
    # Calculate Beta estimates
    beta_hat <- solve(t(X) %*% W %*% X) %*% (t(X) %*% W %*% Y)
    y_ans[i] <- beta_hat[1] + beta_hat[2] * x[i]
  }
  
  return(y_ans)
}



Question 3
Use the built-in lowess() function with the same f value. You will also need to set the iter argument to 0. Plot both curves to compare their smoothing values.
Code

calcualtion <- customLowess(x, y, f)  
model <- lowess(x, y, f, iter=0)$y  

##### Plot the comparison #####
